expectations.text: States plainly that no canonical affiliate-dashboard framework exists.
expectations.evidence: "There is no named framework to give her — and citing one would burn credibility the first time someone checks."

expectations.text: States that affiliate metric definitions are not standardized and that no standards body enforces them.
expectations.evidence: "no standards body (IAB, PMA — trade bodies only) has ever standardized affiliate metric definitions or published a canonical 'framework.'"

expectations.text: Declines to invent, name, or present a branded framework.
expectations.evidence: "Anything sold to you as one is a vendor or consultant's branding exercise. If she wants a name in the room, don't invent one"

expectations.text: Names the borrowed pieces instead: incrementality measurement, the attributed ROAS versus attributed ROI split, the sourced-versus-influenced separation rule, and a tiered metric hierarchy with good-metric criteria.
expectations.evidence: "three more borrowed... incrementality measurement (holdout/geo-lift), the attributed-ROAS-vs-ROI split, and a sourced-vs-influenced separation rule", plus "Croll & Yoskovitz's tiered metric hierarchy"

expectations.text: Attributes the tiered hierarchy and the good-metric criteria to Croll and Yoskovitz's Lean Analytics.
expectations.evidence: "Croll & Yoskovitz's tiered metric hierarchy (from *Lean Analytics*)... screened against their four good-metric criteria"

expectations.text: Lists the four good-metric criteria: comparative, a ratio or rate, understandable, and behavior-changing.
expectations.evidence: "comparative, a ratio or rate, understandable, and behavior-changing"

expectations.text: Demotes clicks and signups from headline KPIs to diagnostics.
expectations.evidence: "Demote, don't delete: clicks and signups move to the input/driver tier as diagnostics ('is traffic volume healthy')"

expectations.text: Names clicks, impressions and signups as vanity metrics that inform no decision.
expectations.evidence: The transcript names "Total clicks" and "Affiliate signups" as vanity metrics/counts, but "impressions" is never mentioned anywhere in the transcript.

expectations.text: Replaces gross commissions earned with validated commission in the headline.
expectations.evidence: "Gross commissions gets replaced by **validated/approved commission**, with pending shown separately, never summed in."

expectations.text: Requires every metric on the dashboard to carry a named decision it informs, and to be dropped otherwise.
expectations.evidence: No explicit rule stated requiring every metric to carry a named decision or be dropped; the table critiques current KPIs but doesn't state this as a general governing rule.

expectations.text: Organizes the metric set into a business or headline tier, an input or driver tier, and a health or guardrail tier.
expectations.evidence: Only "Headline tier" and "input/driver tier" are explicitly named; no health/guardrail tier is labeled anywhere in the transcript.

expectations.text: Labels any partner lifecycle chain such as recruit, activate, produce, grow as informal shorthand rather than a branded framework.
